articles.title: Storm creates huge waves and dangerous currents in southern California
articles.description: Hurricane Marie is creating dangerous conditions at beaches across Southern California over Labor Day weekend, with strong currents and huge waves presenting a threat to swimmers and surfers. Rose Schoenfeld, a National Weather Service meteorologist, said Sunday that Marie stirred up life-threatening conditions as it churned in the ocean hundreds of miles off California’s coast, with some south-facing beaches seeing surf up to 10 feet high. Schoenfeld says rains associated with Marie will fall on parts of Los Angeles County before the storm dissipates. Adam Yacenda, lifeguard battalion chief for the fire department in Newport Beach, says the beach’s lifeguards carried out 177 rescues Saturday.

articles.title: Some cyclists at Bike the Drive dream of safer roads for all
articles.description:
DuSable Lake Shore Drive was a little quieter and whole lot more peaceful Sunday morning.

Thousands of cyclists took part in the 25th Bike the Drive, a once-a-year chance to (legally) bike down 30 miles of state highway and revel in the city's lakefront. Some cyclists said the ride, absent the car noise and congestion, shows how Chicago's streets could be designed safer for walkers and cyclists.

"It's an opportunity to be able to enjoy the full view of Chicago uninterrupted, and it's always a nice day," said Lakisha Tanner, a returning participant who rides her bike regularly around Chicago.

The ride is a fundraiser for the Active Transportation Alliance, a non-profit advocating for better conditions for walking, biking and using public transit throughout the Chicago area. About 20,000 participants come out each year.

Riders had five hours to do the entire 30-mile loop or stick to one section. They could also enter and exit from one of five spots on the route, including the northernmost part at Bryn Mawr Avenue and the southernmost turnaround at 57th Street by the Griffin Museum for Science and Industry. Riders celebrated with coffee, beer and pancakes at a festival in Grant Park.

Mante Eckert, who lives in Dyer, Indiana, came out to Bike the Drive for the third time. Cycling has become an important part of her life. She started riding bikes for her mental health when she was going through a divorce. She bought her first bike back in February after borrowing one for years.

"I love that this event is just a bunch of people doing the same thing together that they love. And everybody is so happy here," said Eckert, 36, sitting in Butler Field after completing her ride. "I cannot think of a better hobby."

Eckert and her sister sometimes spend a weekend day biking the lakefront trail together. She also takes her son out for bike rides. But she wishes Chicago's streets felt safer whenever they ride their bikes off the trail.

She "100% supports" Active Transportation Alliance's mission to improve safety on the road for pedestrians and cyclists.

City transportation officials say they're making the streets less car-centric and safer for cyclists by adding several miles of bike lanes and neighborhood greenways over the last three years.

Advocates say they want those principles applied to the ongoing redesign of the northern leg of DuSable Lake Shore Drive, which was part of Sunday's route. City and state officials released tentative plans to rebuild the eight-lane, lakeside highway generally as it looks today.

But some want planners to consider dedicated bus lanes that would make the highway less driver-focused.

John Draughon also wants to get more people on bikes in Chicago and show them it's possible to get around without a car. He's using a puppet named Zane to spread the word.

The 31-year-old came out for Bike the Drive with Zane strapped over his front wheel. He's working on a YouTube channel, "Zane on the Go," to promote urban mobility and teach people how to navigate public transit.

Draughon wants people to know they don't have to default to driving. When a colleague recently griped about how expensive an Uber is from O'Hare to downtown, he asked why they didn't take the Blue Line. The coworker said they didn't know how.

"I want to encourage people to reduce their car dependency," he said, " and just show them how fun it can be to get to different activities without a car."

Horoscope for Sunday, September 06, 2026
articles.description:
Moon Alert

There are no restrictions to shopping or important decisions today. The moon is in Cancer.

Aries (March 21-April 19)

An average day

Relations with parents and authority figures might be strained today. Resist the urge to be too pushy. Likewise, avoid people who are pushy. Your best choice is to work hard and get better organized. Fortunately, relations with partners are good.

Taurus (April 20-May 20)

An average day

Steer clear of squabbles today, which can easily arise. You might feel criticized, or conversely, you might feel critical about someone else. Certainly, you won't hesitate to express your opinions today. Easy does it. Instead, focus on sports, social outings and fun activities with kids.

Gemini (May 21-June 20)

An average day

Money disputes or quarrels about the ownership of something might arise today. In fact, you have strong feelings about your possessions. Meanwhile, someone older or perhaps a member of a group might think otherwise. Tread carefully. Talk to family members today.

Cancer (June 21-July 22)

An average day

Today the moon is lined up with Mars in your sign at odds with Saturn. This puts a strain on your conversations with others because you might be a tad aggressive and defensive at the same time. This is a poor day to ask for permission or approval from anyone. Just tread water.

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

An average day

Something going on behind the scenes might rankle you today. It might have something to do with the rules and regulations or the law or tradition. Whatever it is, you might want to ignore it or fight it. (You might question the wisdom of this.)

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

An average day

Relations with friends and groups might be tested today, especially about shared expenses or the division of resources or property. You might feel someone is not being fair. They might demand too much of you, or you might think they're not pulling their weight.

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

An average day

This is a tricky day because you like to keep the peace. You enjoy harmony in all your relationships. But today, your relations with authority figures are testy, even aggressive. You might feel criticized, especially by a partner. Don't get your belly in a rash.

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

An average day

Be smart and steer clear of controversial subjects like politics, religion and racial issues because they could quickly explode into an argument. Meanwhile, issues related to your job, your work or even your health seem to be onerous today. Seek solitude in pleasant surroundings.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

An average day

Something to do with socializing, dealing with your kids, vacations, the arts or romance might be disappointing today. Someone might be too opinionated or coming on too strong. (Hopefully this person is not you.) Take it easy and lower your expectations. Be reasonable and forgiving.

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

A so-so day

This is the classic day for irritable conversations and challenges dealing with spouses, partners and close friends. An older family relative or a parent might even be in the mix. Everyone has an opinion, and there's nowhere to run for cover. Send out for dark chocolate.

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

An average day

Although relations with others are aggressive and challenging today, you can still get a lot of work done. (This might be your best option.) Steer clear of negative thinking as well as hurt feelings. Life is short — and fat.

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

An average day

Disputes about money and finances, especially if they cover the cost of a vacation, a social occasion, a sports event or something related to the entertainment or education of children, are likely today. Take your pick. Today has its challenges. Actually, it's the perfect day for a nap.

If today is your birthday

Musician, singer and songwriter Roger Waters (1943) shares your birthday today. You are complex, sensitive, organized, brave and adventurous. You care for the welfare of others. This is a year of learning and teaching. Take time to renew your spiritual beliefs. Explore meditation, prayer or introspection, along with philosophies that provide a better understanding of your life.

articles.title: Indonesia cancels flights as Anak Krakatau volcano erupts
articles.description: Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau volcano has erupted, forcing the temporary suspension of flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. Volcanic ash spread across parts of western Indonesia during the eruption early Sunday. Authorities say the eruption has been ongoing, with ash clouds drifting over the capital Jakarta, Banten, West Java, Lampung and nearby waters. Stranded passengers have sought refunds and retrieved luggage following the cancellation of numerous flights. No casualties or evacuations have been reported. Residents have been advised to stay at least 3 kilometers from the crater. Officials are monitoring aviation risks from the volcano, which trigged a tsunami in 2018 that killed at least 430 people in Sumatra and Java.
